findings.description: The fake checks only the top-level issue fields and itemTypes against the query. It still returns every nested field (`label`, `actor`, `createdAt`, `__typename`) even when the query no longer selects it. So a query mutant that breaks production approval still passes every test. Narrow `answer`'s JSDoc to "only the issue fields `query` selects", or filter the nested node fields too.

`itemType` has exactly one caller (`answer`, line 67), and nothing names a second use. The simpler alternative is to fold it into `answer`'s filter, or to make `timeline` events carry their GraphQL enum value directly, for example a `type: 'RENAMED_TITLE_EVENT'` field next to `__typename`. That removes the helper and its camel-to-snake regex.

process_issues.description: Skipped by gate: security (no trust boundary touched), context (no spec/protocol/infra surface), guards (only test files changed), workflow-safety (no workflow change), maintainability (off the default roster), spec (no closing issue or spec source). Consolidator returned no groups, so 0 findings merged.

The validator confirmed the correctness finding's mechanism but showed it is not a regression: the old fake ignored the query entirely, and the PR's named mutants are all killed. The finding was retagged from important to nit, and its invalid `labels.nodes.name` example was removed, because an empty selection set is rejected by GraphQL.
`gh pr diff` was denied by permissions for the validator. It used `git diff <merge_base>..<head>` on the single changed file instead, which is equivalent here.
